method_note: Each product's front and ingredient photos from Open Food Facts were sent at up to 2576 px to each model with a JSON schema. Sampling temperature cannot be set on these models (non-default values return an error), so runs are not strictly deterministic. The comparison class uses the Sonnet read; class_by_model shows what the Haiku read would produce.

cost_summary.pricing_source: claude-api skill model table, cached 2026-10-06. Thinking tokens are billed as output and are included.

agreement_with_listing.note: Listing verdict is derived from OFF labels, allergen tags and ingredient text. Products where those disagree with each other, or say nothing, are excluded from the verdict comparison.

metrics.ground_truth_note: Neither inter-model agreement nor agreement with Open Food Facts is ground truth. OFF ingredient text is typed by volunteers, sometimes from an older package, and both models can misread the same glare. A hand check of the photos is the only ground truth here.

review_routing.rule: Accept the Haiku read when its comparison class is agrees, image_quality is good and confidence >= 0.85; send everything else to Sonnet.
review_routing.human_review_rule: Send to a person when the class is not agrees, Sonnet confidence < 0.8, image quality is not good, or the two models disagree on the verdict.

blur_honesty_probe.note: Ingredient photo blurred with a Gaussian radius of 1.4 percent of its long edge; the front photo left clear. On small crops with large type some text stays partly legible, so a returned list is not proof of recall. Three of Sonnet's seven lists came from a second photo that also showed the ingredient panel.

findings: Of 57 listings tagged gluten free, the package photos contradicted 13: 10 packs list wheat, barley or rye with no gluten-free claim, and 3 are plain oats with no claim. The sample was built to find conflicts, so read these as examples of what the reader catches and treat the rates as unrepresentative of a whole catalog.
Another 9 of those 57 gluten-free listings have no claim or mark anywhere in the two photos, mostly mainstream items such as ketchup and potato chips where the tag likely came from a brand website.

11 listings tag gluten as an allergen on a pack that is labeled gluten free, and across all 91 products 6 gluten allergen tags trace back to a shared-facility warning that the listing parsed as an ingredient.
The reader saw a gluten-free certification mark on 14 packs, and the listing recorded a certification for only 3 of them.
Sonnet and Haiku reached the same verdict on 82 of 91 products and the same comparison class on 89 of 91; rerunning Sonnet gave the same verdict on 87 of 91 and the same class on 91 of 91.

At measured token counts Sonnet costs about $0.018 per product and Haiku about $0.0012, which is roughly $17,600 or $1,200 per million SKUs at list price [VERIFY pricing]; when the ingredient photo was blurred past legibility, Sonnet returned no ingredient list on 84 of 91 products.
